title: “Justice for Bernardo” vigil outside the Health Ministry
location: Outside the Public Health Ministry, Bissau, Guinea-Bissau
scope: One vigil at the national Health Ministry in Bissau; no evidence establishes a multi-site or nationwide gathering.
participants_original: VOA describes “many Guineans”; the Lusa/RTP report says “dezenas de jovens” (“dozens of young people”). Neither gives an exact number.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. The two read bodies use qualitative terms (“many” and “dozens”) without a number proving 50 or more. The separate Última Hora result claiming more than one hundred people remains search-only because its page returned Cache miss.

start_date.summary: Both read reports place the vigil on 1 February 2021.

end_date.summary: The Lusa report says the vigil lasted about an hour and police dispersed it. As it took place “today” on the report’s 1 February date, the event ended that day; exact time is unknown.

location.summary: Both identify a vigil outside the Health Ministry in Bissau.

scope.summary: The report describes a single vigil before the Health Ministry in Bissau; it does not describe other sites.

organizer.summary: The article does not identify who organized the vigil. It quotes RENAJ vice-president Adama Baldé, which does not establish RENAJ as organizer.

demands.summary: Participants demanded responsibility/justice for Bernardo Catchurá’s death and better hospital conditions, including oxygen; Lusa quotes posters reading “justice for Bernardo” and “we demand oxygen in hospitals.”

participants_original.summary: VOA says “many Guineans”; Lusa says “dozens of young people.” Neither reports a number.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: These qualitative terms do not establish a crowd of at least 50. The unverified CNEWS snippet is not used as evidence.

protester_violence.summary: The read report does not describe violence by participants; no absence is inferred, so unknown.

accommodation.summary: No state accommodation attributable to the vigil is reported; unknown.

arrests.summary: The read report does not establish arrests during the vigil; unknown. The CNEWS arrest claim remains unverified.

beatings.summary: The read report establishes dispersal only, not beatings; unknown. CNEWS force allegations remain unverified.

crowd_dispersal.summary: The Lusa article explicitly says police dispersed the vigil.

ignore.summary: VOA says no government reaction had been reported by publication; silence in this story is not coded as ignore.

killings.summary: Catchurá’s reported death preceded and motivated the gathering; the sources do not report a protest-event killing.

shootings.summary: The read report does not establish gunfire at the vigil; unknown.

notes: The reported death occurred before this gathering and is not coded as a protest killing. The reported oxygen/medical-neglect cause is attributed allegation, not independently established here. VOA’s Lassana Cassamá story and the Lusa report are two distinct reporting outlets; RTP/Lusa is one reporting origin. No exact organizer, turnout number, protester violence, or physical time is established. Search-only CNEWS/Capital News and ANG//VOA reports are discovery leads, not additional verified accounts; the CNEWS “more than one hundred” and force claims were not confirmed.
open_questions: Can a permitted body or other credible contemporary record establish at least 50 participants at this single vigil?
Can the reported “more than one hundred” attendance and alleged baton/kick force be verified from the exact CNEWS article or another source?
Does a source establish arrests, injuries, any further police force, accommodation, or follow-up beyond dispersal?
Does any evidence link the Jan 30 funeral gathering to a continuous episode with this distinct Feb 1 vigil?
